severity_basis: Explicitly requested source policy: a direct known timeout control in an authored PostgreSQL migration requires a matching, immediately preceding reason directive. This is not proof that a timeout is unsafe.

environment.isolation: native run_isolated_corpora; immutable inventories and source bytes verified before/after

representative_source_sample.review_result: All reported lines independently match literal SET/SET LOCAL or RESET of the exact known settings; no known inspected policy false positives. Runtime intent and reason adequacy require review.
representative_source_sample.recall: Not measured on real source; the sample is not a blind domain-intent precision study.

method: Four alternating fresh-process runs; first is process-cold, remaining three warm median. No filesystem cache flush; maximum process RSS, not process-family sum. Shared-VM timings are noisy. Labeled policy sites, not runtime defects.

validation.fix_idempotence: No new SQL fix; qualified directives are unchanged by the existing comment fixer.

unsupported: Dynamic set_config calls and ALTER ROLE/DATABASE policy
RESET ALL and Unicode-escaped parameter names
SQL-standard BEGIN ATOMIC: the whole file abstains
COPY FROM STDIN payloads and following commands
No semantic assessment of whether a reason is adequate
Generated migrations and explicit dumps remain outside the authored-migration policy; this source sample does not include every application dependency.
adoption: Publish first. Preserve existing reviewed debt through the established fingerprint baseline and changed-line ratchet; do not rewrite historical SQL or silently recapture a baseline.
